en: Those who have abandoned the True Dharma.
Homage to the glorious Vajrasattva!
I pay homage to all Buddhas for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings,
for the purification of all karma, and for the pacification of all suffering.

I bow to the noble Sugata, the perfectly awakened Śauddhodani, who has crossed the ocean of existence, and whose compassion for the three worlds reached its end by drying up the sea of suffering for all beings.
Actions do not perish even in hundreds of millions of eons;
having reached the convergence of conditions and the proper time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.
Having committed even a slight evil, the fool goes downward; having committed even a great [evil], the wise man, like one who is homeless, abandons it.
Even a small amount of liquor, when mixed with water, becomes like water; even a great quantity of water, when mixed with liquor, becomes that very liquor.
Even most terrible deeds committed become small through self-restraint.
"I shall speak of their complete uprooting— from revelation and concealment down to the very root.
Mañjuśrī said:
O Blessed One, in future times during the Kali ages, how shall the suffering of sentient beings born from the ripening of evil karma be purified?
The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī! Excellent, excellent, and very well indeed!"
Pay attention; I shall speak:
the sin of killing an Arhat may be [expiated] in twelve years.
One is liberated from the great sin of killing a Brahmin within ten years by means of recitations, meditations, and other such nourishing practices.
One is released from cruel sin through the meditative cultivation of mantra-recitation and other practices;
even having killed a Kṣatriya, one is liberated within eight years.
Sin is purified by the practice of giving and the observance of ethical conduct, and not otherwise;
even for a Vaiśya who has committed a transgression in his sixth year. (15)
It is purified by giving, and especially by restraint.
For those of the Śūdra caste, having killed [one], one is released after five years;
however, by restraining oneself,
the sin perishes, and not otherwise.
Having killed a cow, one becomes a cow-killer;
one is purified after four years by relying on all dharmas and through detachment from all passion.
By this, there is purification from the sins of killing an Arhat and so forth;
likewise, when there is the pulling of hair and so on due to the presence of Cāṇḍālas and others.
Then he is purified by means of moral conduct through three transformations;
however, when one has fallen from those families, he is purified in twenty days.
One is purified by means of the threefold precepts through seven cycles;
by this, purification for those who have fallen from their family lineage and so forth is achieved by relying on a single day, [observing] the time-restriction, the avoidance of meat, and fasting.
Having circumambulated the stūpa, he should go for refuge to the Triple Gem.
On the second day, one should not consume food from the field [of the donor] after having performed the recitation of the True Dharma and the confession of sins and other faults.
Resorting to the third day, one who is free from conceptual construction and has not solicited anything is liberated from all sin through the practice of mantra-recitation and other rites.
Relying upon the fourth day, one should practice fasting;
according to the instruction of the Guru to be contemplated, one should perform this single recitation.
One should constantly bathe [the image] at sacred fords (tīrthas) and by means of constructing shrines (caityas) and the like;
having worshipped according to the prescribed rules, especially through the recitation of hymns (stotra).
The construction of ponds, wells, and canals; the planting of wish-fulfilling trees; and the gift of vehicles for riding such as elephants, horses, donkeys, boats, camels, and carriages.
Land, women, gold, jewels, food, drink, and indeed the gift of fearlessness— these,
as well as even the most terrible deeds committed, are brought to an end through self-reproach;
their total uprooting occurs through both confession and restraint.
I say.
By this, there is purification from the maturation of all evil deeds. Now, the occasion for the practice of the five products of the cow has arrived.
Cow’s urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and water infused with *kuśa* grass—
these are prescribed as the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), which are purifying and cleansers of the body.
The urine of a blue-colored cow is used, curd from a white cow is taken,
and ghee from a tawny cow should be collected.
The destroyer of great sins.
In the absence of [cow dung] from all castes, especially from a Kapilā cow,
one should take one pala of cow urine and one pala of cow dung.
One should offer seven *graha* measures of milk and five *pala* of curd;
one should take one *pala* of clarified butter and one *pala* of water infused with *kuśa* grass.
One should mix cow dung, curd, and clarified butter with water infused with *kuśa* grass;
having proceeded according to the ritual prescribed in the *Kalpa*, one should empower it with the mantra.

The treasure described in the Kalpa should be visualized according to one's inclination; it should be offered together with water from a sacred site (tīrthāmbu) along with the instruction of the Guru.
In this regard, the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ amoghapariśuddhaśodhāya samantena dhīra-aśuddhasatva mahāpadye hūṃ.
One should recite this twenty-eight-syllable mantra one hundred and eight times.
By reciting it twenty-one times, the noble [mantra] destroys great sins.
The Request.
O Greatly Compassionate One, O Lord, for the sake of destroying all evil and for the purification of this impure one, grant me the five products of the cow. (From the *Durgati-*)
O Greatly Compassionate One, O Protector, grant me the five products of the cow,
which arises from all the Victors and purifies all the elements.
"O Great Compassionate One, O Protector, grant me the five products of the cow.
One should offer the five products of the cow by means of the hand of the elder of the assembly. (17)
By this the body is purified; one should give food to the gaṇa and worship them according to one's ability, especially with robes and other such items.
The worshipful [deity] should be honored with the fivefold offerings (pañcopacāra) through devotion of body, speech, and mind;
the ritual acts beginning with the preliminary oblations (prayāja) are considered to be doubled in sequence.
One should cause [the merit] to proceed by means of gifts and interrupt it with circumambulations;
one part should be interrupted by gifts, while another part is interrupted by circumambulations.
For the remaining [deities], the [mantra] is doubled at each successive stage through the practice of recitation, japa, and meditation.
The ritual procedure for purification through confession, which removes the ripening of evil karma for a sentient being extracted from the Noble Tripitaka of the True Dharma, is hereby completed.
The individual empowerment mantras.
Oṃ hūṃ trāṃ hrīṃ khaṃ haṃ.
One should merge [it] with the previously mentioned mantra.
The placement of the five products of the cow.
Having prepared five circles in the center of the ground, one should place cow dung in the middle; there shall be cow urine in the east and curd in the south.
In the west, milk.
In the north, there should be cow's ghee.
And in the center, water with *kuśa* grass. May there be auspiciousness.
